$$

So, they are not upper triangular matrices.

Consider the matrix 
$A=[\begin{aligned}0 & -2 & -7 \\ 2 & -1 & 8 \\ 7 & -8 & 1\end{aligned}].$
Which of the following statements are true?

I. $A$ is upper triangular

II. $A$ is lower triangular

III. $A+{A}^{T}$ is upper triangular
questions.worked_solution:
Let's analyze each statement in turn.

- Statement I is false, since $A$ has non-zero entries below the main diagonal:

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}0 & -2 & -7 \\ 2 & -1 & 8 \\ 7 & -8 & 1\end{aligned}]
$$

- Statement II is false, since $A$ has non-zero entries above the main diagonal:

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}0 & -2 & -7 \\ 2 & -1 & 8 \\ 7 & -8 & 1\end{aligned}]
$$

- Statement III is true, since the result of $A+{A}^{T}$ has all the entries below the main diagonal equal to zero:

$$
A+{A}^{T}=[\begin{aligned}0 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & -2 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 2\end{aligned}]
$$

Therefore, the correct answer is "III only".

canonical_examples.problem:
Which of the following matrices are lower triangular matrices?

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14251131/assets/3bafed1b0b6f3cb02bf32d2c022130802bbb01d4ace620b7ae0541140c3d74a9.svg)
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
The matrix $B$ is a lower triangular matrix since all the entries above the main diagonal are zeros.

The matrices $A$ and $C$ are *not* lower triangular matrices since they each have a non-zero element above the main diagonal:

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{23} & =1\ne 0 \\ {c}_{13} & =1\ne 0\end{aligned}
$$

I. $A$ is upper triangular

II. $A$ is lower triangular

III. $A^T-A$ is lower triangular
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
Let's analyze each statement in turn.

- Statement I is false, since $A$ has non-zero entries below the main diagonal:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14251131/assets/eee380795bf20fca0ede7667e4c9961c9ce1a64705282288a001a355da7cac4d.svg)

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14251131/assets/9f09b99632acf388d210fa1aec94abd6d88820b3974857affcd8243050a22c19.svg)

- Statement III is false, since the result of $A^T-A$ has non-zero entries above the main diagonal:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14251131/assets/1dc153876f81e77ce430f3bc05a71350e055800dec086c32f17653815bf74a15.svg)

Therefore, the correct answer is "II only".

tutorials.problem:
Recall that a matrix is square if the number of rows equals the number of columns. There are other types of square matrices with special names.

- An **upper triangular** matrix is a square matrix in which all entries *below* the diagonal are zeros. For example, the following matrices are all upper triangular matrices:

Note that we can have any number (including $0$) on the diagonal and above.
